key_insight: Entrance vortices create geometry- and Reynolds-number-dependent temperature polarization bias, so a constant entrance correction is inadequate.
engineering_relevance: Lab-scale membrane characterization and heat-transfer correlations should account for inlet geometry and operating Reynolds number to avoid entrance-biased results.
method: Performed 3D CFD simulations of direct contact membrane distillation.
Covered inlet Reynolds numbers from 10 to 1000.
Varied side-chamber length and main-channel height and compared against a straight-channel baseline.
evidence_signal: Simulations showed longer downstream vortex persistence at higher Reynolds numbers, with most geometries shifting from stronger temperature polarization than the baseline at low Reynolds numbers to weaker polarization at high Reynolds numbers.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational findings but no experimental validation; applicability beyond the simulated geometries requires verification.
paper_title: Reynolds-number-dependent entrance bias in temperature polarization of lab-scale membrane distillation
